authors: Ye Xue, Diego Klabjan, Yuan Luo
title: Mixture-based Multiple Imputation Model for Clinical Data with a Temporal Dimension
validity_discussion: Discusses Rubin's multiple imputation framework and replacing missing values with multiple estimates to reflect model variation: "Multiple imputation is originally proposed by Rubin [11] and with the idea of replacing each missing value with multiple estimates that reflect variation within each imputation model."

title: Missing value imputation using deep learning and cluster information in MICE
validity_discussion: Discusses Rubin's MI framework, statistical uncertainty, and Bayesian posterior predictive distributions: "As opposed to single value imputations... multiple imputations generate multiple samples of imputed data sets. The variability across multiple imputed data sets captures the statistical uncertainty in data imputations, improving the imputation accuracy."

authors: Adriana Fonseca Costa, Miriam Seoane Santos, Jastin Pompeu Soares, Pedro Henriques Abreu
title: Missing Data Imputation via Denoising Autoencoders: The Untold Story
validity_discussion: Only defines missing mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and MICE in passing for setup: "There are three mechanisms under which missing data can occur [15]: MCAR, MAR and MNAR... MICE is a multiple imputation technique that specifies a separate conditional model for each feature with missing data."

authors: Brett K. Beaulieu-Jones, Jason H. Moore
title: Missing Data Imputation in the Electronic Health Record Using Deeply Learned Autoencoders
validity_discussion: Mentions MCAR and MNAR mechanisms briefly without substantive theoretical discussion of inferential validity: "The various reasons data may be missing create different types of missing data: missing completely at random, missing at random and missing not at random... Popular multiple imputation methods show particular challenges with data that are not missing at random."

title: TabPFN for Multiple Imputation: Preserving Inferential Validity in Tabular Data
validity_discussion: Provides extensive discussion on inferential validity, Rubin's rules, and uncertainty quantification: "Multiple imputation (MI) provides a widely accepted framework for addressing missing data under valid uncertainty quantification by generating multiple plausible completed datasets, analyzing each dataset separately, and combining results using Rubin's rules to reflect both sampling variability and uncertainty due to missingness."
